cognate: Ved. vīrá- = Av. vīra- = Umbr. ueiro (*wiHro-); Lat. pecua = Umbr. pequo = Av. pasu- = Ved. paśú- (*peḱu-); Lat. salua seruassis = Umbr. salua seritu (same adjective and verb).
drift_or_renewal: At anchor level the pair is split: the AV anchor keeps *wiHro- (vīreṣu) but itemises *peḱu- into species (aśva, go, aja-avi, as RV 1.114.8 does); Cato keeps *peḱu- (pecua) but renews *wiHro- by pastores ('the men who tend them'), whereas Umbrian keeps ueiro pequo intact. The exact pair is attested in support (Av. pasu vīra, AVP paśubhiś ca vīraiḥ, Umbr. ueiro pequo).
phrase: *wiHróm péḱu (*solh₂wó- ser-) 'men and livestock (keep safe)' (pie-lex-wiHros + pie-lex-pekju)
review: The anchors themselves are split. AVŚ 12.2.29 has vīreṣu but itemises the livestock (aśveṣu, goṣu, aja, aviṣu). Cato 141.3 has pecua but pastores for 'men'. The cited support, though, carries the exact two-member cognate dyad in congruent protective prayers: Umbr. ueiro + pequo with salua + seritu (Iguvine VIa 30, 32, verified in Buck); Av. pasu + vīra (Y 9.4, Yt 5.3); Av. θrāθrāi with pasuuā̊ + vīraiiā̊, 'for the protection of cattle and men' (Yt 13); AVP 19.56 paśubhiś + vīraiḥ. Cato's Mars prayer (salua + seruassis) matches the Umbrian verb phrase. Same genre (apotropaic prayer for a community's men and herds), a specific binomial, not a chance pairing. Accepted on the formula; the AV anchor is only a loose instance.

cognate: *h1óḱus 'swift' (Ved. āśú-, Gk ὠκύς) as epithet of the yoked team; with *h1éḱwos in support (Ved. āśúm áśvam ~ Gk ὠκέας ἵππους; Av. āsu.aspa-, recalled).
drift_or_renewal: In the anchor RV 1.118.4b the noun is renewed: the Aśvins' team is 'swift flyers' (āśávaḥ pataṃgā́ḥ, birds serving as horses), but they are 'yoked to the chariot' exactly as ὑπὸ ζυγὸν … ὠκέας ἵππους.
review: Ved. āśú- = Gk ὠκύς and áśva- = ἵππος (*h1éḱwos) are exact. The full pair is in the Vedic support (āśúm + áśvam RV 7.71.5b, 10.107.10a; áśvāḥ + āśávaḥ drawing a chariot, RV 10.119.3b) and matches the Homeric formulaic ὠκέας + ἵππους, here in yoking contexts with ζυγόν (*yewg-) beside Ved. yuktā́saḥ. The anchor RV 1.118.4b has āśávaḥ with pataṃgā́ḥ (birds), a renewal, but the support carries the pair. 'Swift horses' carries some generic risk, but the exact adjective as a stock team epithet in both branches makes this a sound inherited formula.

cognate: *médhu 'mead' (Ved. mádhu, Gk μέθυ, OE medu, ON mjöðr) qualified by *swéh2du- 'sweet' (Ved. svādú/svā́diṣṭha/svā́dman, Gk ἡδύς, OE swēte): adjective + noun with both members cognate in three branches.
drift_or_renewal: Semantic drift of the noun: Gk μέθυ = (sweet) wine, Ved. mádhu = honey/sweet soma-drink, Gmc = mead (the old fermented honey drink). In Vedic the adjective is often in derived/superlative form (svā́diṣṭham mádhvaḥ, svā́dman … mádhūni). In ON the accompanying verb 'drink' is renewed (drekka for *peh3-, cf. Ved. píbati, Gk πίνω), giving 'drink mead' rather than 'sweet mead'.
phrase: *swéh2dus médhu 'sweet mead' (pie-lex-sweh2dus + pie-lex-medhu), with *peh3- 'drink' as verb
review: *swéh2du- + *médhu with both members cognate in three branches: Ved. svādóḥ + mádhvaḥ (RV 1.84.10), svā́diṣṭham + mádhvaḥ (8.49.4), svādv + madhv (AVP 5.28.8); Gk formulaic μέθυ + ἡδύ; OE swētne + medo (Finn. 39). The contexts are congruent: drink at a feast or offering, the host's gift. A honey-drink is naturally 'sweet', which is some generic risk, but the exact adjective-noun pair recurs as a fixed formula in Homer and in Germanic heroic verse. Hávamál 19 has mjöð but no 'sweet' and adds nothing.

cognate: Exact on both words and in the vocative case: Ved. dyaùḥ pítar (vocative with the irregular nominative-form dyaùḥ) = Gk Ζεῦ πάτερ = Lat. Iū-piter (univerbated vocative, the base of the Latin name; Umbr. Iupater, recalled).
drift_or_renewal: none in Greek. In Latin the vocative has fused into a proper name (Iuppiter), used for every case.
review: An exact two-member cognate vocative: Ved. dyaùḥ + pítar = Gk Ζεῦ + πάτερ (= Lat. Iuppiter), the sky-god's name + 'father' in the same case and order, opening a prayer or wish (Il. 17.645 asks him to save the Achaeans; Il. 7.179 is the army's prayer at the lot; Theognis 731). Not generic (a specific divine name with a kin term) and not derivative. The Vedic instance is genuine and the Greek formula is frequent.

words.note: packet maps to pie-root-wekw-speak; vácas- is the s-stem *wékʷos exactly

cognate: Ved. √śru- (śr̥ṇavat, śrāváya, śr̥ṇviṣe) = Gk κλύω (ἔκλυες, ἔκλυε) < *ḱlew-; Ved. vácas- (neuter s-stem) = Gk ἔπος < *wékʷos, with the root noun vā́c- (*wṓkʷs) as variant object in RV 8.96.12d; 1sg possessive Ved. me (enclitic gen.) ~ Gk ἐμόν.
drift_or_renewal: none in the core pair; Vedic alternates vácas-/vā́c-/háva- as object, Greek alternates ἔπος with the bare genitive of the praying person (ἔκλυες εὐξαμένοιο). The worshipper is named by an agent noun of a praise/prayer root in both (Ved. stotúḥ 'of the praiser', Gk εὐξαμένοιο 'of (me) praying'), non-cognate.
phrase: *ḱlew- (aor./subj.) + *wékʷos (acc.) + *me/*h₁eme- 'hear my word' (god as subject, in prayer)
review: Ved. śru- = Gk κλύω (*ḱlew-), with the object Ved. vácas- = Gk ἔπος (*wékʷos, the same neuter s-stem) and a 1sg possessor: Ved. śr̥ṇavat + vácāṃsi + me (RV 1.145.3b, 10.65.13c) and stotúḥ + vácaḥ + śṛṇavat (AVŚ 6.2.1) ~ Gk ἐμόν + ἔπος + ἔκλυες (Il. 14.234 = 16.236). The speech act is the same: the god as hearer of the worshipper's word in prayer. 'Hear my word' has generic risk, but both lexemes are exact, including the specific s-stem rather than an everyday word for 'speech'. RV 7.8.5c and Il. 10.295 have only the verb and are marginal.

cognate: The *gʷʰen- 'slay' word: Ved. han- (áhan, jaghāna, ghnán) ~ OE bana/bona, ON bani 'slayer' (*gʷʰon-, pie-lex-gwhonox). The Germanic anchor (Beo. 2903) supplies only the context and the renewed serpent noun (wyrm). The cognate agent noun is attested in search support from the same episode (Beo. 2825 'Bona ... eorð-draca ... wyrm') and in Hymiskviða 22 'orms einbani', which is my reading of the OCR 'eiribani'.
drift_or_renewal: The serpent noun is renewed in Germanic: OE wyrm / ON ormr (*wr̥mi- 'worm, larva', cf. Lat. uermis) and draca replace *h₁ogʷʰi-; the inherited verb survives as the agent noun *gʷʰonō 'slayer' (bana/bani) rather than as a finite verb. Germanic also keeps the variant where the serpent kills the hero (Beowulf dead 'wyrmes dǣdum', Thor walking nine steps from the serpent and dying), which Watkins counts as part of the same theme (recalled).
phrase: *gʷʰen- *h₁ógʷʰim 'slay the serpent' (pie-lex-gwhenti + pie-lex-h1ogwhis); Gmc. renewal *wurmiz/ *wr̥mi- + *gʷʰonō 'serpent's slayer'
review: All four anchors verified. Vedic side is the textbook collocation: √han- with áhi- as object (RV 1.32.4a, 2.15.1d, 5.31.7b; also 1.32.1c). Germanic: the anchor Beo. 2903 itself has only renewed wyrm and no *gʷʰen- word, so it is context only; the cognate weight is Hym. 22, where OCR 'eiribani' is verified in context as einbani with gen. orms (ON bani < *gʷʰonō, regular). Gen. object + agent noun is a defensible nominalisation of verb + acc. object; serpent noun renewed (ormr/wyrm). Caveat: in Beo. 2825 'bona' is the dragon as slayer of Beowulf, i.e. the relation is inverted, so it is weak support; Völuspá Drepr is not *gʷʰen-. Not generic: bani+serpent in Germanic where the normal kill verbs differ; Vedic and Norse independent.

support: Buck 1904, Oscan-Umbrian grammar §183 (Umbr. voc. Iupater < *Dieu-pater) and Tab. Iguv. VIa (ueiro pequo castruo fri salua seritu)
cognate: Vocative *ph₂ter in prayer: Gk πάτερ = Lat. pater. The theonym *dyew-: Gk Ζεῦ (vocative) = Lat. Iou- (Iouem, in the same sentence as the Mars invocation, not in apposition; packet lists Iouem as unmapped / no content word). The fused Latin vocative Iupiter (Cato 134) and Umbr. Iupater continue exactly *dyeu ph₂ter, as does Ved. dyaùṣ pítar.
drift_or_renewal: In Cato 141.2 the father-vocative has been moved to another god: Mars pater (also Iane pater in Cato 134). Jupiter is named only in the preliminary wine offering (Ianum Iouemque uino praefamino). Spreading 'pater' to other gods is a known Italic development, and the Latin anchor keeps the formula's shape (god + pater vocative + request) with the theonym renewed. Gk ῥῦσαι 'rescue, guard' may belong with Lat. seruare (*ser-u- 'guard'), which would make the petition verbs cognate too, but that etymology is disputed and not relied on here.
phrase: *dyeu ph₂ter (vocative; pie-lex-dyexws + pie-lex-ph2texr) opening a prayer for protection
review: Verified Il. 17.645 (Ζεῦ voc. + πάτερ opening a petition) and CatAgr 141.2-3. The Latin anchor has Mars + pater (theonym renewed; Iouem only in the preliminary wine offering, not in the address), so the anchor alone gives only *ph₂ter. But CatAgr 134.2 (verified) has the fused voc. Iupiter + precor + uti sis uolens propitius, i.e. *dyeu ph₂ter as a vocative opening a petition, matching Ζεῦ + πάτερ (Il. 1.503, 17.645) and Ved. dyaùṣ pítar (RV 6.51.5a); Umbr. Iupater confirmed in Buck. Both elements cognate, same function, Latin and Greek independent at this level. The Mars pater extension is an Italic spread of the title, not evidence against.

cognate: *h1ed- 'eat' (Ved. ad-, Gk ἔδω, ON eta) with *krewh2- 'raw flesh/gore' (Ved. kravís, Gk κρέας, ON hrár 'raw'); Ved. āmá- 'raw' = Gk ὠμός (support: Il. 22.347 ὤμ' … κρέα ἔδμεναι, an exact *h2eh3mo- + *krewh2s + *h1ed- match to āmaṃ … kraviḥ adanti).
drift_or_renewal: ON hrár keeps the root as the adjective 'raw' while the noun is renewed (kjöt 'meat'); Gk κρέας generalised from 'raw flesh' to any meat, so rawness is expressed by ὠμός or implied (Cyclops). 'Human' is renewed per branch (Ved. pauruṣeya- from púruṣa-, Gk ἀνδρόμεος from ἀνήρ) but the notion 'human flesh' is shared by the AV and Od. 9 passages.
phrase: *h2eh3mom krewh2s h1ed- 'eat raw flesh' (pie-lex-h2eh3mos + pie-lex-krewh2s + pie-root-h1ed-eat)
review: Verified AVŚ 8.6 (āmá- + māṃsá- + ad-, with kravís- in the same verse, of flesh-eating demons), Od. 9.297/347 (κρέας + ἔδω/φαγεῖν of the Cyclops), Il. 22.347 (ὠμός + κρέας + ἔδμεναι, verified), and the Edda prose/verse lines with hrár + eta. Three exact equations: āmá- = ὠμός (*h₂eh₃mó-), kravís- = κρέας (*krewh₂-), ad- = ἔδω (*h₁ed-); ON hrár continues the same *krew-root as adjective. Context congruent: raw-flesh eating as the mark of savagery/monstrosity (also compound ὠμηστής, Il. 24.207, ~ Ved. āma-/kravya- 'eater' compounds). Generic risk is real since all three are basic words, but the triple, fixed in a negative frame, goes beyond chance. Weakest leg: Norse (only 'raw' + 'eat', vikings, not monsters).

cognate: Agent noun *déh₃tor- 'giver' (Ved. dātár-, Av. dātar-, Gk δωτήρ/δώτωρ) governing the genitive plural of *h₁wesu- 'good (things)': Ved. vásūnām, Av. vohunąm, Gk ἑάων. Gk ἑάων occurs in Homer only in δωτῆρες/δῶτορ ἑάων and in Il. 24.528, where the same genitive plural depends on δίδωσι 'gives' (Zeus's jar of goods), i.e. the verbal correspondent of the agent-noun phrase.
drift_or_renewal: In the packet Vedic lines the genitive object is renewed: rāyáḥ ... dātā́ (RV 6.23.10d, rayí- 'wealth' for vásu-) and figura etymologica dātrásya dātā́ 'giver of the gift' (RV 9.97.55c); the old vásūnām survives in RV 8.51.5a and in Avestan vohunąm dātārō. In Il. 24.528 the agent noun is replaced by the finite verb δίδωσι, a natural verbal transform of 'giver of goods'.
phrase: *déh₃tores h₁wesuHom 'givers of good things' (pie-root deh₃- + *h₁wésu-), predicated of the gods
review: Verified Il. 24.528 (δίδωσι + gen. pl. ἑάων), RV 6.23.10d and 9.97.55c (dātár- with renewed genitives), and support Od. 8.325 θεοί + δωτῆρες + ἑάων, Od. 8.335 δῶτορ + ἑάων, Hes. Th. 46/111, RV 8.51.5a dātár- + vásūnām, Y65.12b and VrS27.12a vohunąm + dātārō, Y16.1b. Exact equation in all three: agent noun *deh₃-tor- + gen. pl. of *h₁wesu-, predicated of gods. ἑάων is an otherwise dead archaism in Greek, which excludes chance. The packet's Vedic anchors renew the genitive; the exact Vedic form is in support.

cognate: In the wider formula: Lat. pecua = Umbr. pequo = Av. pasu = Ved. paśu- (*péḱu); Umbr. ueiro = Av. vīra- = Ved. vīrá- (*wiHro-). In the packet itself: Lat. domo (*dóm-) ~ Av. nmāne (*dm-) 'in/for the house' as the locus of the blessing; Lat. salua seruassis = Umbr. salua seritu (exact Italic cognate pair).
drift_or_renewal: Cato renews *wiHro- with pastores 'herdsmen' (Umbrian keeps ueiro); the Avestan Shnuman passage renews *peḱu with gav- 'cattle' (gə̄ušca vąθβa 'herds of cattle') beside vīra-, and AVP 19.53.35 spreads the pair into gavām aśvānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ. Renewal of one member while the dyad and its function persist is exactly what is expected of a fixed merism.
phrase: *wiHro- *peḱu (+ *dem- 'house') as object of a prayer for protection: 'keep safe men and cattle (of my house)'
review: Anchors verified. CatAgr 141.2-3 has pastores + pecua + salua + seruassis for the household (pecua = *peḱu; *wiHro- renewed by pastores). The Avestan anchor (gav- + vīra-) and the AVP anchor (gavām aśvānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ in the context line) renew the cattle word and are weak in themselves. The claim stands on the verified support: Umbr. ueiro + pequo + salua + seritu (Buck, Tab. Ig. VIa) and Av. pasu + vīra (Y9.4e), with YtFra θrāθrāi + pasuuā̊ + vīraiiā̊ 'for the protection of cattle and men': both elements cognate, the same protective-prayer function, Italic and Iranian independent. The Umbr. seritu = Lat. seruassis match is intra-Italic only. Same grade as C050.

cognate: *n̥-mr̥tó- 'immortal' as the standing epithet and substitute for 'gods': Ved. amŕ̥ta- (RV 7.4.5b amŕ̥tān = the gods; devā́ amŕ̥tāḥ is frequent, 23 RV pādas) ~ Gk ἄμβροτος (θεὸς ἄμβροτος, Il. 24.460, Il. 22.9; recalled as an exact equation). Its counterpart is *mr̥tó-/*mórto- 'mortal' = humans: Ved. márta- (RV 6.16.32c) ~ Gk βροτός (Od. 1.66). Lat. deus ~ Ved. devá- (the Greek god word θεός is not cognate).
drift_or_renewal: Greek usually renews ἄμβροτος as ἀθάνατος in this slot (Od. 1.67 θεοῖσιν ἀθανάτοισιν, the context line after the anchor) and keeps ἄμβροτος mostly for divine substances. Latin immortalis is a fresh formation (-āli-) on mort-, not the old *-tó- adjective. Both renewals are formally transparent, which is why the slot survives.
review: Anchors verified (RV 7.4.5b amŕ̥ta- for the gods; RV 6.16.32c márta-; Od. 1.66-67 βροτός vs ἀθάνατος + θεός; Cato Orig. dii + immortales). Exact equation Ved. amŕ̥ta- = Gk ἄμβροτος (*n̥-mr̥tó-) as the epithet of gods (RV 10.66.13d devá- + amŕ̥ta-; Il. 24.460 θεός + ἄμβροτος, verified), set against *mr̥tó-/*mórto- 'mortal' used as a noun for humans (márta- ~ βροτός, same root, different ablaut). Two cognate elements in the same gods-vs-mortals polarity. Greek mostly renews the epithet with ἀθάνατος, as in the Od. 1.67 context line. Latin immortalis is a fresh formation and possibly a Greek calque, so acceptance rests on Vedic and Greek. Generic risk is medium, since gods are commonly called 'deathless'.

cognate: The packet line h.Cer. 375 itself gives only ἵππους + ὄχεσφιν; 'immortal' (ἀθανάτους) stands in the adjacent context line 376, and the exact cognate ἄμβροτοι ἵπποι is only in support (Il. 16.381). Equation: *h1éḱwos (aśva ~ ἵππος) with 'immortal': Ved. amṛ́ta- = Gk ἄμβροτος < *n̥-mr̥tó- (support Il. 16.381 ἵπποι ἄμβροτοι); plus *weǵh- in the chariot (Ved. vahanti ratham; Gk ὄχεσφιν, ὄχος < *wóǵhos).
drift_or_renewal: In the packet anchor Greek uses ἀθάνατος (the productive replacement of ἄμβροτος in the same sense) in the next line (376); the exact cognate ἄμβροτοι ἵπποι survives in Iliad 16. Vedic 'chariot' is rátha- where Greek uses ὄχος (cognate with Ved. vah-/vā́ha-): the convey-root is kept in the noun in Greek and the verb in Vedic.
phrase: *n̥mr̥tóes h1éḱwōs 'immortal horses' (pie-lex-nmrtos + pie-lex-h1ekjwos) drawing the god's chariot (*weǵh-)
review: AVŚ 13.1.47 verified: the bay horses of the Sun, amŕ̥ta-, draw his chariot. The Greek anchor HH Cer. 375 lacks the adjective; ἀθάνατος (renewed) is in line 376. The exact equation is in verified support: Il. 16.380-381 ἵπποι + ἄμβροτοι (Achilles' god-given horses). Both elements are exact cognates (*h₁éḱwos = áśva-/ἵππος; *n̥-mr̥tó- = amŕ̥ta-/ἄμβροτος), in attributive agreement, of divine teams. Medium generic risk: 'immortal' is freely applied to divine things in both traditions. The ὄχος/vah- part is incidental.

cognate: Lat. pecua/pecus = Ved. paśu- (support; in AVŚ 4.21 the cattle are the addressees) = Umbr. pequo = Av. pasu- (*péḱu); the human member *wiHro- survives in Ved. vīra- (RV 1.114.8), Umbr. ueiro, Av. vīra-.
drift_or_renewal: Packet anchors renew both members in places: Ved. go- for paśu-, Lat. pastores/familia for *wiHro-; the averting verbs are not cognate (Ved. pari-vṛj, dūraṃ nī vs Lat. prohibere, defendere, auerruncare, salua seruare = Umbr. salua seritu).
phrase: *wiHrōs péḱu (pie-lex-wiHros + pie-lex-pekju) 'men (and) cattle' as object of a prayer that a god avert harm
review: The same *wiHrō- + *peḱu- protective formula as C036, so the same grade. It is true on verified support: Umbr. ueiro + pequo + salua + seritu (Buck) and Av. θrāθrāi + pasuuā̊ + vīraiiā̊ (YtFra2.10e, 12.4e), with both elements cognate in protective prayer. This claim's own anchors add little: AVŚ 4.21.14 and AVP 19.14.24 have gó- 'cow', not paśu-, and no vīra-; CatAgr 149.2 is a legal clause in a pasture-sale contract, not a prayer; the averting verbs are not cognate; the Mars-Rudra parallel is typological only. RV 1.114.8 (gó-, áśva-, vīrá-) is Vedic-internal.
